definitions.explanation: A milky-textured skincare product used to moisturize the skin, typically applied after toner in a Japanese skincare routine.
A milky white fluid produced by certain plants, or an emulsion in chemistry.

examples.japanese: {化粧水|けしょうすい}の{後|あと}に{乳液|にゅうえき}をつける。
examples.english: I put on moisturizing lotion after toner.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{乾燥|かんそう}するので、しっかり{乳液|にゅうえき}で{保湿|ほしつ}したほうがいい。
examples.english: It gets dry in winter, so you should moisturize well with lotion.

examples.japanese: ゴムの{木|き}から{乳液|にゅうえき}を{採取|さいしゅ}する。
examples.english: To extract latex from a rubber tree.

examples.japanese: {植物|しょくぶつ}の{茎|くき}を{切|き}ると{白|しろ}い{乳液|にゅうえき}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: A white milky sap came out when I cut the plant's stem.

examples.japanese: タンポポの{茎|くき}を{折|お}ると、{乳液|にゅうえき}がにじみ{出|で}るのを{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}に{見|み}たことがある。
examples.english: I remember seeing milky sap seep out when breaking a dandelion stem as a child.

notes:
USAGE:
In everyday use, sense 1 (skincare product) is far more common. Japanese skincare routines typically follow a sequence: {洗顔|せんがん} (face wash) → {化粧水|けしょうすい} (toner) → {乳液|にゅうえき} (moisturizing lotion). The botanical/chemical sense (sense 2) appears in scientific texts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {乳液|にゅうえき}を{塗|ぬ}る (to apply lotion)
- {乳液|にゅうえき}をつける (to put on lotion)
- {保湿|ほしつ}{乳液|にゅうえき} (moisturizing lotion)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {化粧水|けしょうすい}: toner, face lotion — a lighter, water-based product applied before {乳液|にゅうえき}
- クリーム: cream — thicker moisturizer, applied after {乳液|にゅうえき}
